messages.subject: Spec function
parts:
Hi,


I’m doing this little exercise:


a <- readWave(file=file.choose(),header=FALSE)
 
enva = env(a, norm = FALSE, envt="abs")
amp_value = mean(enva)

speca = spec(a, norm = FALSE)
amp_value = mean(speca[,2])

I was expecting to get similar absolute amplitude values from both methods. 
As I understand it the mean of env(a) provides de average absolute amplitude of my recording. As spec(a) second column gives the amplitude per frequency band from my recording, should not the mean of this column give a similar result, i.e. the recording absolute amplitude average? 

However, results differ in three orders of magnitude (716.7 vs. 187464.4)


Why amplitude values from spec are higher?


Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Spec function
parts:
Hello,

Using env() and meanspec() cannot give similar results in terms of energy. The equivalent of energy between the time and frequency domains is not direct. It is ruled out by the Parseval's theorem that you can check with:

data(tico)
time <- sum(tico@left^2)
fspec <- Mod(fft(tico@left))
N <- length(fspec)
frequency <- 1/N*sum(fspec^2)
time - frequency

HTH

Jerome
